messages:
devon: Heads-up — saw a flurry of SIGTERM on tiny inference pods in ap-southeast1b ~02:13 UTC. Suspect prebind queue timeouts + network hiccup causing cascade. @maria @aj please take a look :eyes:
maria: On it. Which node pool? Any grafana links?
aj: I have traces — prebind latency jumped to ~45s for a subset of nodes in pool-7c, scheduler started backoff and evicted pods that were short-lived. I can paste traces.
devon: Node pool-7c, yes. High conn drops from that AZ to control plane for ~30s. We then saw scheduler retries piling up. Short-lived pods (1-2min) are getting SIGTERM before they even start real work.
sophia: Ugh. That explains customer errors this morning. Do we have kubelet logs showing PreBind failures?
devon: Paste of kubectl describe pod (snippet):
```
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning PreBind    1m    kube-scheduler     prebind failed: binding timeout after 30s
  Normal  Scheduled  1m    kube-scheduler     Successfully assigned default/inf-small to node-7c-12
  Warning Failed     0s    kubelet            Failed to sync pod: network timeout
```
maria: scheduler metrics show schedule_attempt_duration_seconds P95 spiking to 40s for that period. Also see kube-apiserver auth latency bump.
kyle: Any admission webhook timeouts? Those can block binding too.
aj: We checked — no webhooks slow. It's mostly API connection retries from kubelets and scheduler RPC to apiserver.
devon: Hypothesis: transient network egress issue from pool-7c -> apiserver load balancer. When control plane RPCs slow, scheduler prebind path stalls, pods linger in the bind window and hit our eviction window for short pods.
sophia: Mitigations? Increase PreBind timeout? That feels risky. Maybe we can raise the short-pod grace window or detect network flare and pause eviction for pods in prebind state.
maria: For immediate relief, I can push a conservative bump: scheduler prebind timeout to 60s for ap-southeast1 rollout only. Rollback if it causes backlog. Thoughts?
kyle: Sounds OK as temp fix. Also suggest adding a metric alert on bind queue length + apiserver lat spikes so SRE can page earlier.
aj: I’ll add a scheduler flag rollout RFC after the hotfix. Also adding a workaround in node pool autoscaling: temporarily cordon affected nodes if kubelet RPC error rate > threshold.
devon: Good. Action items: 1) @maria apply 60s prebind timeout to ap-southeast1 canary (5 nodes) now. 2) @aj open RFC for safer prebind/backoff handling + eviction grace logic. 3) @kyle add alert: schedule_queue_length > 50 for 2m AND apiserver_request_duration_seconds P95 > 1s -> page. 4) infra-bot: annotate incident ticket with node-pool-7c timeline.
infra-bot: Incident 2026-03-apse1b-007 created and linked to thread.
maria: Patch applied to canary subset, watching.
devon: Thanks — initial canary looks stable, fewer SIGTERMs. Keep monitoring for 15m, then we can widen if healthy.
sophia: I'll notify CS for affected customers and include ETA for rollback if regressions.
aj: RFC created: "scheduler-prebind-resilience" link: https://go/repo/rfc/1234
devon: Great job team. Follow-up: investigate root network cause with cloud provider (possible egress NAT flapping). Closing updates in 1h unless we see further regressions.
